sourceState: Uncommitted working-tree follow-up; no commit or push was made.

findings.summary: Compose previously supplied published fixed JWT/mock-payment secrets to an API running with NODE_ENV=production and used a published database password.
Login rate limiting used req.ip without configuring the single Nginx proxy hop, so Compose clients could share one limiter key.

changes: Compose requires POSTGRES_PASSWORD, JWT_SECRET, and MOCK_PAYMENT_SECRET; the production API rejects missing, short, and known published development/CI JWT or mock-payment values.
Compose binds web and PostgreSQL host ports to 127.0.0.1 by default; API trusts only the configured number of proxy hops, set to one for the Nginx-to-API Compose path and zero by default.

npm run env:compose writes independent random values to a Git-ignored .env, does not print secret values, refuses overwrite, and refuses to generate a new DB password when the current Compose project volume exists.
The isolated DAST runner generates independent ephemeral DB/JWT/mock-payment secrets and assigns loopback host bindings for each uniquely named project.
